metadata.title: Machine learning evidence from PISA 2018 data to integrate global competence intervention in UAE K–12 public schools

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 student questionnaire data and constructs a per-student academic performance output by averaging plausible values (PVs) across reading, mathematics, and science after applying PV-specific weighted averaging within each PV. The manuscript does not report whether complex survey sampling weights (e.g., student/school weights) were applied in the CatBoost training or in the SHAP aggregation, so weight usage for population-representative estimation is unclear. The authors do, however, explicitly apply PV weighting logic (weighted average within each PV, then mean across PVs) to obtain unbiased performance statistics. Because the model is trained with CatBoost and interpreted with SHAP, the paper does not describe any additional complex-survey adjustments (e.g., replicate weights or BRR/JRR), which may affect generalizability and uncertainty quantification.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used publicly available PISA 2018 data for students enrolled in UAE K–12 schools (public and private). The model input uses student questionnaire responses only (global competence indicators from the questionnaire); global competence cognitive test data were not used because the UAE did not participate in the cognitive test. Features with more than 50% missing data across the whole dataset were excluded. The analytic dataset contains 600,821 student rows and 80 survey-feature columns, and the output is a per-student academic performance score derived from PISA 2018 cognitive-test PVs for reading, mathematics, and science.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (UAE and OECD countries) — student questionnaire global competence; academic performance (reading, mathematics, science PVs)
main_findings.target_variable: Academic performance score (mean of PVs across reading, math, science)
main_findings.performance_metrics: CatBoost validation: RMSE = 47.74, MAE = 37.2, R² = 0.75. SHAP used for feature contribution; no additional predictive metrics reported for SHAP-based subgroup comparisons.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged self-efficacy on global issues, awareness of global issues, and awareness of intercultural communication to predict students’ academic performance score (averaged across plausible values for reading, mathematics, and science), finding that these three global competence indicators contributed meaningfully to performance while the other three indicators contributed less. This indicates that strengthening global competence—especially self-efficacy and intercultural awareness—may be a practical lever for improving academic outcomes and informing targeted UAE K–12 intervention design, though the SHAP-based evidence is predictive rather than causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 student questionnaire data for UAE K–12 students (public and private schools) and compares patterns with other PISA 2018 participating countries (OECD members). It predicts a per-student academic performance score defined as the mean of plausible values (PVs) across reading, mathematics, and science, and trains a CatBoost boosted-regression-tree model (70/30 train/validation split; 2,000 estimators; depth 10; learning rate 0.05). Model validation performance is RMSE = 47.74, MAE = 37.2, and R² = 0.75. Using SHAP TreeExplainer, the authors find that three global competence indicators—self-efficacy regarding global issues (GCSELFEFF), awareness of global issues (GCA_WARE), and awareness of intercultural communication (AWACOM)—show stronger positive contributions than the other three indicators. The paper does not report whether complex survey sampling weights were applied in the ML training, and SHAP feature importance is not causal evidence, so policy implications should be framed as predictive guidance rather than causal effects.
